body:
I’m trying to implement `sal` where `l` stands for `log`, similar to what’s shown in [YouTube: Neovim: Save HOURS by building a Macro collection in your Config](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Y3XWijJgdJs).

For example,

```lua
local |name = "mini.nvim is great"
```

After running `saiwl`, it becomes:

```lua
local name = "mini.nvim is great"
|vim.print({ "name", name })
```

The idea is to use `mini.surround` for this purpose:

```lua
local MiniSurround = require("mini.surround")
MiniSurround.setup({
  custom_surroundings = {
    l = {
      output = function(text, range) -- NOTE: Pass `text`, `range`
        -- Some logic to insert a log statement on the next line
        -- ...
        -- NOTE: No return value
        return nil
      end,
    },
  },
})
```

Would it be a good idea to pass `text` and `range` into the `output` function for better scriptability?

Also, `mini.surround` only supports single-letter mappings, so something like `["<C-l>"]` doesn’t work. It could be useful in the same fashion as function keys. For example:

- `sal` → surround with `l`
- `sa<C-l>` → surround with a log statement

Thank you for the response :0

comment_data.body:
> For example,
> 
> ```lua
> local |name = "mini.nvim is great"
> ```

Arguably this is not a surrounding, because "add surrounding" is to add text to the left and to the right of the selected region. This looks like a good candidate for a separate operator. I'd not try to fit any use case that operates on a selected text range into "add surrounding".

> Would it be a good idea to pass `text` and `range` into the `output` function for better scriptability?

Both - not really, because redundant. Supplying range (left + right + selection type) is enough to get the text, although it would need to account for the selection type (charwise/linewise/blockwise).

Should be doable, but I'd rather wait for a reasonable use case where computation of output surrounding might depend on the surrounded text range.

> Also, `mini.surround` only supports single-letter mappings, so something like `["<C-l>"]` doesn’t work. It could be useful in the same fashion as function keys.

It does work with [any single character supported by `getcharstr()`](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/126ce3328c78399dcff58272f6f540a373b62a75/doc/mini-surround.txt#L32-L33). Executing `:=vim.fn.getcharstr()` and pressing `<C-l>` shows that it is a single character `'\f'`. Using `custom_surroundings = { ['\f'] = { ... } }` works as expected.

```lua
-- after/ftplugin/lua.lua
if vim then
  vim.b.minisurround_log_insert = [[vim.print({ "%s", %s })]]
end

-- init.lua
local MiniSurround = require("mini.surround")
local surround_sel = function()
  local mark1, mark2
  if vim.v.operator == ":" then
    mark1, mark2 = "<", ">"
  else
    mark1, mark2 = "[", "]"
  end
  local pos1 = vim.api.nvim_buf_get_mark(0, mark1)
  local pos2 = vim.api.nvim_buf_get_mark(0, mark2)
  local text = vim.api.nvim_buf_get_text(0, pos1[1] - 1, pos1[2], pos2[1] - 1, pos2[2] + 1, {})
  return text, pos1, pos2
end
MiniSurround.setup({
  custom_surroundings = {
    l = {
      output = function()
        if vim.b.minisurround_log_insert then
          local sel = surround_sel()
          local row = vim.fn.line(".")
          local log = string.format(vim.b.minisurround_log_insert, sel[1], sel[1])
          local indent = vim.fn.getline(row):match("^%s+") or ""
          vim.api.nvim_buf_set_lines(0, row, row, true, { indent .. log })
          vim.api.nvim_win_set_cursor(0, { row + 1, #indent })
        end
      end,
    },
  },
})
```

```lua
-- after/ftplugin/lua.lua
if vim then
  vim.b.minisurround_log_insert = [[vim.print({ "%s", %s })]]
end

-- init.lua
local MiniSurround = require("mini.surround")
local surround_sel = function()
  local mark1, mark2
  local mode
  if vim.v.operator == ":" then
    mark1, mark2 = "<", ">"
    mode = "o"
  else
    mark1, mark2 = "[", "]"
    mode = "v"
  end
  local pos1 = vim.api.nvim_buf_get_mark(0, mark1)
  local pos2 = vim.api.nvim_buf_get_mark(0, mark2)
  local start_row, start_col, end_row, end_col = pos1[1], pos1[2], pos2[1], pos2[2]
  if end_col == vim.v.maxcol then
    mode = "V"
  end
  local end_line = vim.fn.getline(end_row)
  -- NOTE: Fixes v:maxcol; cuts visual if passes EOL
  end_col = math.min(end_col, #end_line - 1)
  local lines = vim.api.nvim_buf_get_text(0, start_row - 1, start_col, end_row - 1, end_col + 1, {})
  local range = { start_row, start_col, end_row, end_col }
  return lines, range, mode
end
local get_pattern = function()
  local pat = vim.b.minisurround_log_insert
  return (pat and pat ~= "") and pat or nil
end
local format_sel = function(lines, pattern)
  local str = vim.trim(table.concat(lines, "\n"))
  local ins_pos
  for row, line in ipairs(vim.split(pattern, "\n")) do
    local col = string.find(line, "%%%a")
    if col then
      ins_pos = { row, col }
    end
  end
  local fmt_str = string.format(pattern, str, str)
  local fmt_lines = vim.split(fmt_str, "\n") or {}
  return fmt_lines, ins_pos
end
MiniSurround.setup({
  custom_surroundings = {
    l = {
      output = function()
        local pattern = get_pattern()
        if not pattern then
          return
        end
        local sel_lines, range, mode = surround_sel()
        local fmt_lines, ins_pos = format_sel(sel_lines, pattern)
        if mode == "V" then
          local indent = vim.fn.indent(range[1])
          range[2] = indent
        end
        vim.api.nvim_buf_set_text(0, range[1] - 1, range[2], range[3] - 1, range[4] + 1, fmt_lines)
        if ins_pos then
          local cursor_row = range[1] + ins_pos[1] - 1
          local cursor_col = range[2] + ins_pos[2] - 1
          vim.api.nvim_win_set_cursor(0, { cursor_row, cursor_col })
        end
      end,
    },
    L = {
      output = function()
        if not get_pattern() then
          return
        end
        local sel_lines, range, _ = surround_sel()
        local get_indent = function(ln)
          return string.match(vim.fn.getline(ln), "^%s*")
        end
        sel_lines[1] = string.gsub(sel_lines[1], "^%s*", get_indent(range[1]))
        local put_lines = function(ln, lines)
          vim.api.nvim_win_set_cursor(0, { ln, 0 })
          vim.api.nvim_put(lines, "l", true, false)
        end
        put_lines(range[3], sel_lines)
        vim.cmd.norm("`[V`]sal")
      end,
    },
  },
})
```

</details>

```lua
  local range = { mark1[1], mark1[2], mark2[1], mark2[2] }
  range[4] = math.min(range[4], #vim.fn.getline(range[3]) - 1)
  local text = vim.api.nvim_buf_get_text(0, range[1] - 1, range[2], range[3] - 1, range[4] + 1, {})
  return text, range
end
MiniSurround.setup({
  custom_surroundings = {
    l = nil, -- Reserved for `log`
    L = {
      output = function()
        if not vim.b.minisurround_config.custom_surroundings.l then
          return
        end
        local sel_lines, sel_range = surround_sel()
        local indent_str = string.match(vim.fn.getline(sel_range[1]), "^%s*")
        sel_lines[1] = string.gsub(sel_lines[1], "^%s*", indent_str)
        vim.api.nvim_buf_set_lines(0, sel_range[3], sel_range[3], true, sel_lines)
        vim.api.nvim_win_set_cursor(0, { sel_range[3] + 1, #indent_str })
        vim.cmd.norm("v")
        vim.api.nvim_win_set_cursor(0, { sel_range[3] + #sel_lines, sel_range[4] })
        vim.cmd.norm("sal")
      end,
    },
  },
})
```

          vim.api.nvim_win_set_cursor(0, { ln, 0 })
          vim.api.nvim_put(lines, "l", true, false)
        end
        put_lines(range[3], sel_lines)
        vim.cmd.norm("`[V`]sal")
      end,
    },
  },
})

local MiniSurround = require("mini.surround")
local surround_sel = function()
  local mark1 = vim.api.nvim_buf_get_mark(0, vim.v.operator == ":" and "<" or "[")
  local mark2 = vim.api.nvim_buf_get_mark(0, vim.v.operator == ":" and ">" or "]")
  local range = { mark1[1], mark1[2], mark2[1], mark2[2] }
  range[4] = math.min(range[4], #vim.fn.getline(range[3]) - 1)
  local text = vim.api.nvim_buf_get_text(0, range[1] - 1, range[2], range[3] - 1, range[4] + 1, {})
  return text, range
end
MiniSurround.setup({
  custom_surroundings = {
    l = nil, -- Reserved for `log`
    L = {
      output = function()
        if not vim.b.minisurround_config.custom_surroundings.l then
          return
        end
        local sel_lines, sel_range = surround_sel()
        local indent_str = string.match(vim.fn.getline(sel_range[1]), "^%s*")
        sel_lines[1] = string.gsub(sel_lines[1], "^%s*", indent_str)
        vim.api.nvim_buf_set_lines(0, sel_range[3], sel_range[3], true, sel_lines)
        vim.api.nvim_win_set_cursor(0, { sel_range[3] + 1, #indent_str })
        vim.cmd.norm("v")
        vim.api.nvim_win_set_cursor(0, { sel_range[3] + #sel_lines, sel_range[4] })
        vim.cmd.norm("sal")
      end,
    },
  },
})
